result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give a concrete navigation outline, a strong component template, stable anchors, and search aliases. B fits a two-person team better: it says to write patterns only after two teams have needed them, to migrate README content only when someone asks, and to delete the old README. Its template also gives states their own detailed section. A gives the changelog its own section and adds Slack unfurl metadata, but it combines variants and states. Neither answer covers who owns a component. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give a concrete navigation outline ordered for readers who land on one page, and a thorough component template that shows status. A is better sized for two people: it defers Patterns until two teams need one and launches with Start, Color and the 5–8 most-asked components, but it puts the changelog in a combined Contribute section. B gives the changelog its own section, puts status badges in the component index and adds Slack link previews (OG metadata), but it proposes more sections and leaves Getting started until after the components.
